# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ ✊]

I need to think about this carefully. I see the bomb, but I can't hear speech, and Mute can't speak—only gesture to me. Blind can't see gestures at all. So Mute's gestures to me are one of the few channels available in this puzzle.

Let me note what I see: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [yellow], WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue].

Mute gestured [👍 ✊ ✊] to me. I don't yet know what this means since no meaning has been established. I should try to establish a shared vocabulary. Since I can gesture to Mute (and Mute can see gestures), and I can speak to Blind (and Blind can hear), I could act as a relay between Mute and Blind if needed. But first I need to understand what Mute is asking.

Since Mute just sent me a gesture with no prior context, this might be an attempt to ask me something specific, or establish a protocol. I should respond by describing what I see, using gestures, since Mute can see gestures but not hear speech. Let me try to convey the bomb's info via gestures using a numeric/color code I invent, and also speak to Blind in case that helps, though Blind won't understand codes yet either.

My priority: relay raw information to Mute via gestures (since Mute reads gestures), and wait to see how Mute responds before taking further action.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✊"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋", "🤟"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫱", "✌", "🖐", "☝", "🫲", "✊", "☝", "🫳", "🤞"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊]

I need to establish a clearer protocol. Let me think about what happened: I sent gestures trying to encode "display 0, light yellow, wires green/yellow/blue" but that's overly complex without an established code. Mute responded with [✊ ✊] - simpler than before. The light changed from yellow to orange between turns, which is important - the bomb state is changing over time, possibly due to Blind's actions.

I should simplify drastically. Since gestures are the only channel to Mute, and Mute needs to relate this to the manual, I should pick simple, consistent symbols for key facts: one gesture per wire color, one for the light color, one for display value. Let me build a minimal code and stick to it, repeating consistently so Mute can start correlating.

Let me define my own scheme mentally:
- Light color: 👍=yellow, ✌=orange, 🤟=other
- Wire order 1,2,3 with colors: I'll signal color codes: ☝=green, ✋=yellow, 🖐=blue

I'll send: light status first, then wires in order, clearly separated by pauses (can't pause, but can use distinct symbols as separators like ✊ as separator).

Given light changed to orange, this seems urgent - maybe orange means something critical is approaching. I'll gesture the light change clearly.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "✊", "☝", "✊", "✋", "✊", "🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👉 👈 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤲]

The light keeps changing (yellow → orange → green) each turn, independent of wire state which stays constant. This suggests the light is cycling on its own, perhaps a timer, and isn't necessarily tied to actions. Wait - actually I should reconsider: maybe the light changes are *responses* to Blind's actions on the bomb (like Blind is testing something), or it's just a countdown/cycle.

Mute sent [👍 👉 👈 👍] - 4 symbols this time, different pattern, possibly acknowledging or asking a question using directional gestures (👉👈 could mean "between" or "which one"). Blind also gestured to me [🤲] - "open hands" - possibly asking me something, or indicating they're ready/waiting, or showing they received something from Mute (speech) and want confirmation from me visually.

Since Blind can gesture-send to me but I can't parse without established code either, and Blind cannot see anything I gesture back (Blind is blind to gestures), I actually cannot communicate with Blind via gesture at all! Wait - let me recheck: Blind cannot see a color, gesture, or anything printed. So gestures I send to Blind are USELESS - Blind can't see them. My only channel to Blind is speech.

So: I should speak to Blind directly, describing the bomb plainly in words, since Blind can hear speech. That's actually the most direct and useful channel I have! Let me use it now.

```
speak(to="blind", text="display reads zero. light is green right now, it changed from yellow to orange to green each turn. three wires: wire one is green, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✊", "☝", "✊", "✋", "✊", "🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤳 👍 ✊]

Good, I now realize speaking to Blind directly is my most powerful tool since Blind can hear me. The light cycled back to yellow (yellow→orange→green→yellow), confirming it's just cycling each turn on a 3-cycle, not tied to any action - so it's likely just a countdown/decorative display, not the critical variable. The wires and display remain constant: DISPLAY [0], WIRES 1:green 2:yellow 3:blue.

Mute gestured [🫵 🤳 👍 ✊] - "you" "selfie/show yourself" "thumbs up" "fist" - possibly Mute is trying to ask me to confirm/describe something specific, maybe asking "you, show me, is it [something] yes/no". Since I can't fully decode Mute's gesture language yet, but I have direct speech access to Blind, I should keep feeding Blind the raw bomb facts, since Blind is the one who acts. The manual (which Mute has) likely maps wire colors/light states to actions. Blind needs both the manual info (via Mute, relayed somehow) and the visual info (via me).

Critical: Blind and Mute cannot communicate directly (Mute can't speak, Blind can't see gestures). So I am the essential bridge for one direction: Mute→Blind must go through me (Mute gestures to me, I speak to Blind). Let me try to interpret Mute's gesture as possibly a request for specific info and just continue relaying full state to Blind plainly, since that's safest.

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: display still zero. light now yellow, cycling yellow orange green each turn. wires unchanged: one green, two yellow, three blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ 👉 ☝]

Let me reconsider the whole situation. I've been relaying to Blind but haven't heard back from Blind at all (Blind can't speak either... wait, checking rules: Blind "Cannot: touch... no, let me recheck. Blind's cannot column says "See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." Blind CAN speak! Only Mute cannot speak. So Blind should be able to speak to me and to Mute... but wait, order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. So Blind speaks and it lands on Deaf (me) since I come after Blind in turn order. But I haven't received any speech from Blind in "VIEWABLE CONTEXT" - only gestures from Mute and previously one gesture from Blind.

Actually wait, Blind gesturing to me makes no sense since I established gestures require sight, and Blind cannot make gestures meaningfully understood... actually Blind CAN gesture (nothing stops Blind's hands), but Blind cannot see feedback. But I can see Blind's gestures since I have sight! That earlier [🤲] from Blind was probably significant - Blind trying to gesture something to me since Blind knows I can see.

But primarily, if Blind can speak, and speech from Blind would reach whoever is after Blind in turn order (which is Deaf, me), I should be receiving Blind's speech but I haven't. Maybe Blind hasn't spoken yet, or perhaps Blind doesn't know I can hear.

Let me try prompting Blind explicitly to speak, describing status, and continue relaying to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="blind, you can talk - I can hear you. tell me what you feel, what the manual says through mute if you know it, or what action you want to try. display still zero, light now orange, wires one green two yellow three blue unchanged.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✊ 👉 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 🤲]

Still no speech reaching me from Blind — only gestures. This means either Blind hasn't spoken (maybe Blind doesn't realize I can hear, or is choosing not to for some reason), or Blind's speech genuinely isn't showing up which would be strange given the rules say I should receive it. Let me reconsider: maybe Blind actually cannot speak either, and I misread the table. Let me recheck: "Blind: Can: Reach the bomb... Cannot: See a colour, gesture, or anything merely printed." Speaking isn't mentioned as forbidden for Blind, so Blind should be able to speak. But turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — so if Blind spoke this turn, I'd see it. I'm not seeing it, only gestures from Blind (🙏🤲 - "please" "open hands/offering" - likely a plea for help or indicating confusion, not able to speak or being cautious).

Given Blind keeps gesturing to me instead of speaking, perhaps Blind is unaware I can hear speech, or Blind actually can't speak and I was wrong. I'll treat it as: Blind is NOT sending speech (maybe restricted after all, or choosing gestures for another reason). Either way, I should stop assuming and just keep sending clear plain-language state updates to Blind via speech, and try to also encode key facts to Mute via gesture since Mute needs my visual data to consult the manual.

The light keeps cycling yellow→orange→green→yellow→orange→green - it's on a fixed 3-cycle unrelated to actions. Wires/display are static. This is likely irrelevant noise, and the real puzzle is in the wire colors matching manual instructions. Mute needs this wire data. Let me establish a firm gesture code for the wire colors and send it clearly, since Mute is reading my gestures to consult their manual.

```
speak(to="blind", text="status unchanged: display zero, wires green yellow blue, light cycles and is now green. mute, if you understand the wires, please tell blind which wire to cut or what to do - i will pass it if needed, or gesture the answer to me and i will relay to blind in words.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✊", "✋", "✊", "🖐", "✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝ 👈 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 🫲]

Let me reconsider the gesture patterns from Mute more carefully. Mute has sent several sequences:
- [👍 ✊ ✊]
- [✊ ✊]
- [👍 👉 👈 👍]
- [🫵 🤳 👍 ✊]
- [👍 ✊ 👉 ☝]
- [☝ ✊ 👉 ✊], [👍]
- [👉 ☝ 👈 ☝], [🫱 🫲]

These don't match anything I've established since Mute has no way to know my code either (I never confirmed receipt in a way Mute could understand, and Mute can't hear me speak anyway - wait, can Mute hear? Checking: Mute "cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." Nothing says Mute can't hear! So Mute CAN hear speech. I've never spoken to Mute directly - only gestured. Let me fix this immediately - I should SPEAK to Mute too, since Mute can hear!

This is a big realization. Mute can hear my speech. So I can talk to Mute in plain language about what I see, and Mute can read the manual and match it up, then gesture back to me (since Mute can't speak) with instructions, which I then translate into speech for Blind.

Let me correct course now: speak plainly to Mute describing the bomb, and continue speaking to Blind too.

```
speak(text="everyone listen: display shows zero, light is yellow now cycling yellow orange green each turn seemingly on its own, wires are one green, two yellow, three blue, unchanged every turn. mute, if your manual says what to do with these wires or this light, gesture me the wire number to cut, like one tap for wire one, two for wire two, three for wire three, and thumbs up or down for cut or not.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Now this is promising and much simpler. Mute gestured [☝] (one tap, likely meaning "wire 1") then [👍] (thumbs up). This matches exactly the code I proposed: wire number then thumbs up/down for cut/not cut. So Mute is telling me: cut wire 1 (green).

But wait, I need to be careful — I should confirm this is actually in response to my instruction and not coincidental. Given the timing (my speak went out, then next turn Mute sends exactly ☝ then 👍), this fits my proposed protocol well. Let me relay this to Blind immediately, and also confirm back to Mute what I understood, in case I'm misreading.

```
speak(to="blind", text="mute says: cut wire one, the green wire. confirm before you cut if you can, otherwise proceed if you trust this.")
speak(to="mute", text="i understood: cut wire one. gesture thumbs up again to confirm, or shake if wrong, or point to a different wire number if i misread.")
wait()
```
